html:
SMTO-LLM-0086 — Your model's web address isn't valid

GUID: 4f3fa006-30e1-43e5-b9a9-9580b11ad820
Slug: model-endpoint-invalid
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • The address SMTO uses to reach your model service isn't a usable web address, so SMTO couldn't send any request to the model.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and open the Main card, or whichever card shows the problem. The Endpoint box on that card holds the web address SMTO uses for that model.
  2. In Endpoint, enter the full address starting with http:// or https://, with the computer's name or number and port, usually ending in /v1 (for example http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1). Select Save Main. SMTO needs a complete address with the right beginning and port to find the service.
  3. Select Check saved model. It confirms SMTO can now reach the model at the new address.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model shows your model's name and passed.

If it still fails

  • Ask the person who runs your model service for its exact address, and send them the copied error details. Don't turn off certificate or password checks to get it working.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The configured model base URL failed validation before any request: it is not an http or https URL, has no host or an invalid port, or contains a # fragment.

What this means

  • SMTO must construct Chat Completions requests from a base URL. A missing host, unsupported scheme, invalid port or fragment prevents reliable routing before inference.

Why this can happen

  • SMTO must construct Chat Completions requests from a base URL. A missing host, unsupported scheme, invalid port or fragment prevents reliable routing before inference.

How to diagnose it

  • The configured model address is not a valid HTTP or HTTPS endpoint.
  • A normal request reaches the corrected endpoint and returns a valid response.

How to fix it

  • Set Endpoint on the role card in Settings › Setup › Model routing to the provider's base URL with http:// or https://, a host and the correct port, normally ending in /v1 (for example http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1). Do not enter a /chat/completions or /responses request URL, and remove any # fragment.
  • Correct Mission Control → Model Configuration → LLM endpoint URL to the provider base URL, normally ending in /v1. Use its actual host and port; do not enter a chat/completions or Responses request URL.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • A normal request reaches the corrected endpoint and returns a valid response.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
